# 西舫彙征

**ID:** X1551
**Volume:** X78
**Category:** 史傳部類
**Original Category:** 史傳部／淨土宗
**Byline:** 清 瑞璋輯
**Dynasty:** 清
**Date:** 1644–1911
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X1551

## Contributors
- 瑞璋 (A001457)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 2-juan mid-Qīng Pure-Land biographical anthology, the title of which puns on the canonical metaphor of the **Western Skiff** — Amitābha's *jiē-yǐn* "welcoming-and-conducting" boat that ferries devotees from the saṃsāric ocean to the Western Pure Land. The image is taken from a verse cited in the work's preface: "*shēng-sǐ máng-máng gǔ dù-tóu / Mítuó bō-dòng jì-rén zhōu*" — "Through the busy ferry-crossings of the past, Amitābha works the saving-boat for those crossing." The compiler **Ruìzhāng** 瑞璋 was a Qīng Pure-Land monk who collected biographical materials from across the prior tradition and added contemporary materials, with the explicit aim of providing "fellow members of the Lotus Society" (*lián-shè fǎ-lǚ* 蓮社法侶) with exemplary models for their own Pure-Land practice.

**Abstract**

The work is a compendium of c. **150 brief biographies** in 2 juan, drawn primarily from [KR6r0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0074), [KR6r0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0075), [KR6r0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0076), [KR6r0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0078), and (probably) [KR6r0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0080) — i.e., the standard *wǎngshēng zhuàn* tradition — supplemented by mid-Qīng material. The arrangement is chronological and the prose terse, suggesting a target-readership of practising lay Pure-Land devotees rather than scholars. Internal references suggest a composition in the Dàoguāng / Xiánfēng period (c. 1820–1860).

The text is preserved in the **Jiāxìng** 嘉興 canon (J) supplement and in the Manji Xuzangjing (X78 no. 1551). It is one of several **regional Pure-Land compendia** of the mid- and late-Qīng — alongside [KR6r0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0083) *Xiūxī wénjiàn lù* of [咫觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%92%AB%E8%A7%80) — that document the persistence of the lay-Pure-Land subculture into the late-imperial period.
